title: How to Receive Money From Canada to India (2026 Guide)
summary: Learn how to receive payments from Canadian clients in India. Compare CAD receiving methods, fees, exchange rates, settlement times, and required documents.
body_markdown:
## **How Much Does It Cost to Receive Payments From Canada?**


The cost of receiving a payment from Canada can include several charges. Before choosing a provider, check which of these apply:


-


**Transaction fee:** A fixed amount or percentage charged to process the payment.


-


**Currency conversion:** The exchange rate used to convert CAD into INR, including any markup.


-


**Bank charges:** Fees charged by the sending, intermediary, or receiving bank.


-


**Withdrawal fee:** A charge for transferring money from a payment platform to your Indian bank account.


You may not pay all four. Some providers include certain costs in their quoted fee, while others charge separately. Ask for the total cost of your chosen payment route so you can estimate how much will reach your account.


### **CAD to INR Example**


Suppose your Canadian client pays CAD 5,000 and the exchange rate is ₹65 per CAD. Before fees, that works out to ₹3,25,000.

## **Should You Invoice Your Canadian Client in CAD or USD?**


Invoice in the currency agreed with your client. CAD may be the practical choice if your client pays in Canadian dollars, while USD may make sense if your contract already uses US dollars.


Before sending the invoice, check four things:


-


**Your client's payment options:** Confirm which currency they can send and whether their bank charges for conversion.


-


**Your provider's terms:** Check the currencies it accepts and any conversion or withdrawal fees.


-


**Payment date:** If your client pays later, the exchange rate may change before you convert the funds.


-


**Your agreement:** Make sure the invoice currency matches the payment terms in your contract.


Also check the route the money will take. If a CAD payment is converted into another currency before reaching your account, you may incur an additional conversion cost.


## **How Long Does It Take to Receive Payments From Canada?**


The transfer time depends on the payment method, the banks involved, and any verification checks. Incorrect details, public holidays, or requests for supporting documents can delay the payment.

These are general estimates, not guaranteed delivery times. Check the provider's current settlement terms before promising your client a payment date.


## **What Documents Do You Need to Receive International Payments?**


The documents you need depend on your business structure, the payment, and your bank or provider's requirements. Keep these records available in case they are requested.


-


**Invoice:** Identifies the client, amount, currency, and reason for payment.


-


**Contract or work order:** Supports the purpose of the transaction where required.


-


**Identity and tax details:** Such as PAN or other documents requested during verification.


-


**Payment confirmation:** Helps trace a delayed transfer.


-


**Bank statement or remittance record:** Shows the amount credited and any deductions.


-


**Foreign-exchange documentation:** Such as a FIRA, where issued or applicable.


You may not need every document for every payment. Ask your bank or provider what applies to your transaction, and retain the relevant records for accounting and tax purposes.


## **What is FIRA, and Do You Need It for Payments From Canada?**


A Foreign Inward Remittance Advice (FIRA) records details of a[foreign inward remittance](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/understanding-foreign-inward-remittances-for-businesses-in-india) . It can help support your records when you receive money from overseas clients.


Whether you receive a FIRA depends on the payment route and the institution processing the transaction. Some providers arrange remittance documentation for eligible withdrawals.


A FIRA is not the same as an invoice or a tax certificate, and it does not by itself determine whether the income is taxable. Check with your bank or accountant which documents they need for your transaction.


### **What is a Purpose Code?**


A purpose code identifies the reason for a foreign-exchange transaction. The correct code depends on the payment's purpose, such as services you provided or goods you exported.


Choose a code that accurately describes the transaction. If you are unsure which one applies, check with your authorised dealer bank or payment provider. The[Infinity Purpose Code Finder](https://tools.infinityapp.in/purpose-code) can help you identify a possible code to verify.


## **What Should You Know About FEMA Reporting and Taxes?**


India's Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 took effect on 1 October 2026. The RBI's recent clarification addressed reporting for certain personal transactions, but this should not be treated as a blanket exemption for freelancers earning business income from overseas clients.


Eligible small exporters may use a self-declaration instead of an invoice for bills up to ₹10 lakh, subject to the applicable process. This is not a general exemption from reporting requirements. Check the[RBI clarification](https://www.business-standard.com/finance/news/personal-service-transactions-need-no-reporting-under-new-fema-rules-rbi-126100701282_1.html) and confirm your requirements with your authorised dealer bank.


Tax is separate from FEMA reporting. Overseas income may be taxable in India, while GST depends on the nature of the supply and the applicable export-of-services conditions. Consult a tax professional if you are unsure how these rules apply to your business. For more details, read our[Export Declaration Form guide](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/export-declaration-form) .


## **Why Has Your Payment From Canada Been Delayed or Rejected?**


A payment may be delayed or rejected because of incorrect account details, missing information, a compliance review, or restrictions on the payment method.


**Check these common causes:**


-


**Incorrect bank details:** Verify the beneficiary name, account number, and[SWIFT/BIC code](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/bic-swift-code-meaning-and-role) .


-


**Missing payment information:** Your bank may request an invoice, contract, or explanation of the payment's purpose.


-


**Unsupported currency or transfer method:** Confirm that your receiving account accepts the currency and type of transfer your client used.


-


**Intermediary bank delays:** Ask the sending bank for a transfer reference so it can trace the payment.


-


**Pending verification:** Complete any identity, business, or transaction checks requested by your provider.


If the payment is rejected, ask the bank or provider for the reason and confirm whether the money has been returned. Do not ask your client to send it again until the status of the original transfer is clear.

## **Frequently Asked Questions About Receiving International Payments From Canada to India**


### **1. What is the best way to receive money from Canada to India?**


It depends on how your client prefers to pay, the amount, and the total cost. A local CAD receiving account suits clients who prefer local transfers, SWIFT works for direct international bank payments, and a payment link makes online payments easier.


### **2. Can I receive Canadian dollars directly into my Indian bank account?**


That depends on your bank and the payment route. Some transfers are converted into INR before they are credited, while eligible foreign-currency accounts may receive CAD. Confirm the supported currency and conversion process with your bank or provider.


### **3. How much does it cost to receive CAD 1,000 in India?**


There is no single fee for every provider; it may range from CAD 5 to CAD 35. The amount you receive depends on the transaction fee, exchange rate, and any bank, intermediary, or withdrawal charges. Check the applicable fees and rate before accepting the payment.


### **4. Do I need a FIRA to receive money from a Canadian client?**


The available documentation depends on the payment route and the institution processing the transaction. Ask your bank or provider whether it issues a[FIRA](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/fira-vs-firc) or another remittance record and which documents you should retain.


### **5. Are payments from Canadian clients taxable in India?**


They may be. Income-tax treatment depends on your circumstances, while GST treatment depends on the nature of the supply and whether the applicable export-of-services conditions are met. Seek professional advice if you are unsure how your income should be treated.


### **6. How long does a transfer from Canada to India take?**


SWIFT transfers often take 1-5 business days, but this is not guaranteed. Local transfers and payment links follow their own processing and settlement timelines, generally 24 hours to 5 days. Bank checks, public holidays, and incorrect details can delay a payment.
